newsitem.title: USA: New games from Parker Bros. and Milton Bradley.
newsitem.headline: New games from Parker Bros. and Milton Bradley.

text.p: You've got battling raptors, masterpiece auctions and chickens that lay plastic eggs. Add to that updated versions of popular board games and you've got the newest toys and games from Parker Brothers and Milton Bradley.
Introduced at a recent "games day" in New York, the toys and games range from low-tech board games fuelled by brain power to sophisticated hand-held, battery-driven toys.

For young children, there is the indoor-outdoor game, "Chicken Croquet." Players have to hit a light platic ball through two wickets and then hit the chicken. When hit, the chicken jumps, squawks and lays an egg. The first one with two eggs wins (MB, $21.99, ages 4 and up, mid-June).

Based on the popular character Arthur, "Arthur Goes to the Library Game" (MB, $9.99, ages 4 and up, July) helps children develop memory and matching skills, as the player who amasses the most Arthur books wins.

New for 1997 is the "Star Wars Millennium Falcon Space Shooter" (MB, $19.99, ages 5-10, available). Using a shooter shaped like the space vehicle, each player tries to knock down the Imperial Empire's forces with as few Space Shotter discs as possible.

The popular board game "Monopoly" has morphed into "The Monopoly Game: Star Wars Edition" (PB $29.99, ages 8 and up, available). Instead of houses and hotels, claim your property with X-wing fighters, Millennium Falcons, Tie Fighters and Star Destroyers.
"The Empire Strikes Back Customised Card Game" recreates a battle between the Light Side and the Dark Side (PB, $14.99, ages 9 and up, available).

Tied in with the movie, "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," the "Jurassic Park Board Game" pits humans against dinosaurs (MB, $14.99, ages 7 and up, available). The electronic hand-held game, "Final Flight," (MB, $14.99, ages 6 and up, available) puts the player on a helicopter to save people down below. Hand-held "Raptor Run" (MB, $19.99, ages 6 and up, mid-June) has players trying to escape the raptors and make it to safety.

Raptors battle head-to-head in "Battling Raptors." (PB, $19.99, ages 5 and up, available) Each player has a dinosaur and the object is to kick the opposing dinosaur off its pedestal. First one to dismount the other raptor gets the point.
"The Lost World: Jurassic Park Card Game" (PB, $4.99, ages 3 and up, available), players draw cards to be either humans or dinosaurs, and must bag their prey to win.

Compete with the commands from an electronically powered wand to "bop it," "twist it" or "pull it." The goal of "Bop It" (PB, $19.99, ages 8 and up, July) is to keep up with the commands until you lose.
Electronic hand-held "Sorry" pits a player against three computer opponents. They are out to get you. (PB, $14.99, ages 6 and up, June)
"Jumanji" is another hand-held electronic game. The player has to earn letters, collect weapons and defeat the Jungle Dangers (PB, $14.99, ages 6 and up, July).

For girls who admire the magical powers of teenaged witch Sabrina, there is "Sabrina the Teenage Witch Board Game" (PB, $9.99, ages 7 and up, June). Find out how much Sabrina really knows about you. Are you a secret jock, geek or freak?

Brain power fuels "Scrabble Up," a twist on the classic word game. A vertical gameboard and a timer turn it into a race against an opponent for the most words and points (MB, $14.99, ages 8 and up, available).

It helps to know celebrities, motion pictures and popular culture to play "Planet Hollywood The Game." Two teams answer questions about entertainment, and the last team to respond before a "Plant Hollywood" timer goes off, wins (MB, $24.99, ages 12 and up, July).

Fooling people, and getting away with it, is the theme of "Beyond Balderdash," an update of the original bluffing game. (PB, $24.99, ages 10 and up, available) The new game features categories including words, movies, people, initials and dates.

You too can own a Renoir or a Picasso, but make sure it's not a fake. That's the idea behind "Masterpiece," (PB, $14.99, ages 8 and up, available) where players bid for works of art and try to spot forgeries. The player with the greatest fortune wins.

The newest in the series of "Trivial Pursuit" games is "Trivial Pursuit Genus IV Edition" (PB, $29.99, adult, available). This edition features a new collection of questions from the game's classic categories.
